 WECT INVESTIGATES: Pender County submits audit to state after months of delays, missed deadlines 
 Pender County has attributed the delays to staffing vacancies and inexperience. By Connor Smith Published : Nov. 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM EST | Updated : 10 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PENDER COUNTY, N.C. (WECT) - Pender County has submitted its annual financial audit to the state after months of delays and missed deadlines. 
 As previously reported by WECT Investigates, the county risked losing up to $140,000 in state sales tax revenue distributions after missing a June 30 deadline, outlined under state law, to submit its FY2025 audit to the Local Government Commission (LGC). 
 The county had also received a notice of noncompliance earlier this year, but took until November to submit the audit, despite the contract with Hickory-based auditor Martin Starnes & Associates saying it would be finalized by Dec. 31, 2025. 
 During a meeting Monday night, commissioners received a presentation about the audit from the firm. According to the presentation, the audit found problems with the county’s books, including significant audit adjustments that were made, lack of controls over the vendor payment process and the late submission of the audit.
 The lack of controls is tied to the scam that stole more than $650,000 in public money last year, county leaders confirmed. The SBI and FBI opened investigations after that incident, which County Manager Colby Sawyer later said was the result of county staff not following procedure .
 The county had previously attributed the submission delay to senior finance staff leaving late last year, leaving staff “inexperienced” with handling audits, along with three finance positions sitting open.
 “With the finance department short three positions, all tasks are taking longer than normal, but all three positions are being filled with new employees starting over the next month, so we anticipate timelines to improve and workloads to decrease,” the county said in June. 
 On Monday, county leaders said that because of the delay with the 2025 audit, the 2026 audit likely won’t be done by the end of December, the original due date outlined in the contract. Finance Director Meg Blue said staff are doing their “very best” to finish it by the end of December, though the audits usually take three months of work. 
 Sawyer said during Monday’s meeting that steps taken to address the issues identified in the audit have included giving staff more specific roles and timelines to follow during the auditing process, adding a three-step verification process for vendor changes, and regularly comparing budgets with what was actually spent. 
 “We would certainly want no findings, and are certainly working towards that,” Sawyer said Monday. 
 Commissioners voted Monday to approve a new $128,500 contract with Martin Starnes & Associates. A copy of the contract notes the 2026 audit will be delayed because of the late completion and submission of the 2025 report. 
 Pender County had paid the firm $92,890 for the 2025 audit fee, and according to state law, up to 150% of that cost could be withheld in sales tax revenue. That number would be roughly $140,000 for Pender County. 
 A spokesperson for the Local Government Commission didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday clarifying if any revenue was withheld from the county. A Pender County spokesperson had previously indicated they were going to be successful in appealing for a delay in any withholdings.
